name: Etorphine
summary: Etorphine (M99) is a semi-synthetic opioid possessing an analgesic potency approximately 1,000–3,000 times that of morphine. It was first prepared in 1960 from oripavine, which does not generally occur in opium poppy extract but rather the related plants Papaver orientale and Papaver bracteatum. It was reproduced in 1963 by a research group at MacFarlan Smith in Edinburgh, led by Kenneth Bentley.

pharmacology.text: Etorphine is a potent, non-selective full agonist of the μ-, δ-, and κ-opioid receptors. It has a weak affinity for the nociceptin receptor.

uses.text: Etorphine is available legally only for veterinary use and is strictly governed by law. It is often used to immobilise elephants and other large mammals. Diprenorphine (Revivon) is an opioid receptor antagonist that can be administered in proportion to the amount of etorphine used (1.3 times) to reverse its effects. Veterinary-strength etorphine is fatal to humans.
